solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: American could be someone arriving at JFK by Virgin

parts.note: the Virgin is Mary, mother of Jesus
a plane passenger touching down at the New York airport is one who lands, a lander

explanation.surface: A traveller flying into New York on a Virgin airline flight might well be an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Virgin' looks like the airline but is the Virgin Mary. 'could be' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the US state of Maryland is an American.

clue.text: A notice about poison

indicators.note: about here means moved around, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning notice concerning poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges A NOTICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, or monkshood, is a plant yielding a deadly toxin.

clue.text: Long time before start of night

parts.note: a year is a period of time

indicators.note: start of takes just the opening letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A long while passes before nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to pine or crave it, a synonym.

clue.text: Great tie, unusually decorative item

indicators.note: unusually signals that the letters of the phrase appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: Praise for a striking necktie as an unusual ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges GREATTIE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aigrette is an ornamental plume or spray of gems worn on a hat or in the hair.

clue.text: Maybe one could actually sell ice to an Eskimo!

definitions.text: Maybe one could actually sell ice to an Eskimo!

parts.words: Maybe one could actually sell ice to an Eskimo!
parts.note: selling ice to Eskimos is the proverbial impossible sale, but ice is slang for diamonds, which a gem dealer really does sell

explanation.surface: A tribute to a supersalesman who could sell ice to an Eskimo.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom praises a persuasive seller; 'ice' is also underworld slang for diamonds, so a gem trader does it literally.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer in precious gems sells 'ice' to anyone, Inuit customers included, so the idiom becomes literal.

clue.text: Hill going up given X — bad!

indicators.note: in a down clue going up means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: a tor is a rocky hill, especially on Dartmoor
X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A hill climb marked with an X, a bad result.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going up' turns TOR into ROT. A tor is a craggy hill in south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Rotten is a common synonym for bad, of food or behaviour.

clue.text: Enchanting Liberal — just a bit smooth-tongued

indicators.note: just a bit says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A charming Liberal politician who is perhaps a little too slick in speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Glib describes fluent but insincere speech, the same as smooth-tongued.

clue.text: Lake surrounded by cunning ornamental borders

indicators.note: surrounded by puts the lake word inside the cunning word

parts.note: guile is craft or cunning
loch is the Scottish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A lake ringed by artful decorative edging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cunning' is a noun here, not an adjective describing the borders; 'surrounded by' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Guilloche is an architectural ornament of interlaced bands, used for borders and mouldings.

clue.text: Heron is flying away from the water

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent scattering into a new order

explanation.surface: A heron takes flight away from the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges HERONIS. 'Away from the water' means towards land, not out at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Inshore means close to or towards the coast rather than out to sea.

clue.text: The old woman backing firm in an unhealthy state

indicators.note: backing here means supporting from behind, so the old woman comes after the firm

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm
ma is a familiar word for one's mother, the old woman

explanation.surface: A mother propping up a company that is in poor financial health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' looks like a reversal signal but only places MA behind CO.
explanation.definitionFit: A coma is a prolonged state of deep unconsciousness, a serious medical condition.

clue.text: Sight least awful or most awful?

indicators.note: awful here says the letters are in a terrible mess and must be reordered

explanation.surface: A puzzled question whether a view is the least or most dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges SIGHTLEAST; 'or' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Ghastly means horrible or dreadful, so the superlative is the most dreadful.

clue.text: Intended to join female at the match?

definitions.text: Intended to join female at the match?

parts.words: Intended to join female at the match?
parts.note: an intended is a betrothed man, and a match is a marriage, where he joins his bride

explanation.surface: Someone planning to meet a woman at a football game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Intended' reads as a verb and 'match' as a sporting fixture; in fact the intended is a man promised in marriage, and the match is the wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: An engaged man is someone's intended, who will be joined to his bride.

clue.text: Neglect sees maiden maybe left with nothing, all right?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored
O looks like zero, nothing
OK means all right

explanation.surface: A neglected young woman left with nothing asks whether things are fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maiden' is the cricket term: a maiden is an over (six balls) yielding no runs. 'sees' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: To overlook something is to fail to notice or attend to it, to neglect it.

clue.text: Socialist took steps, being blue- pencilled?

parts.note: red is a familiar label for a socialist
to take steps is to act, past tense acted

explanation.surface: A left-wing activist took action and was censored.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is a link word. A blue pencil is the editor's traditional tool for cutting text.
explanation.definitionFit: Redacted text has been edited or censored, as an editor's blue pencil strikes out passages.

clue.text: Daughter needs to put a bit of weight on, woman at first declared

indicators.note: at first puts the woman's name at the front of the answer
in a down clue putting the daughter on the weight places her letter underneath it

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
an ounce is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A woman announces her daughter must gain a little weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needs to put' is linking; 'on' sets D below OUNCE, and 'at first' puts ANN at the top.
explanation.definitionFit: To announce is to proclaim or declare publicly.

clue.text: Dear French instructor spilling drink

indicators.note: spilling means losing the drink, so those letters are dropped from the word

parts.note: a teacher is an instructor
tea is a drink

explanation.surface: A beloved French teacher knocks over a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spilling' removes TEA from TEACHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cher is the French word for dear, as in a letter's greeting.

clue.text: Church books badly produced with staplers

indicators.note: badly produced suggests the letters have been put together wrongly, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Hymnals poorly bound using office staplers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly produced' rearranges STAPLERS; 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A psalter is a book containing the Psalms, used in church services.

clue.text: Relation called, last character to come forward

indicators.note: the final letter is moved up to the front of the word

parts.note: rang means telephoned, called

explanation.surface: A relative phoned and the last person in the queue is asked to step up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last character to come forward' moves the G of RANG to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Gran, short for grandmother, is a family relation.

clue.text: Wild animal getting eggs on grass turned over

parts.note: roe is fish eggs

indicators.note: turned over means the word is flipped, reading backwards

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass

explanation.surface: A wild creature eating eggs on grass that has been flattened.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' turns REED into DEER; 'getting' and 'on' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The roe deer is a small wild deer of Europe and Asia.

clue.text: Wind first thing in the morning? Set to swirl in

indicators.note: in puts the swirled letters inside the other word

parts.note: first thing in the morning is early

indicators.note: to swirl suggests the letters are whirled into a new order

explanation.surface: A wind whips up at dawn and begins to swirl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to swirl' scrambles 'Set' to STE, which 'in' places after the second letter. 'Wind' is a noun here.
explanation.definitionFit: An easterly is a wind blowing from the east.

clue.text: Alluring female terribly rebellious, putting off characters in bus

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are badly jumbled and need rearranging
putting off says the letters of the next word are removed from the pool before rearranging

explanation.surface: An alluring woman so unruly she puts people off on the bus.
explanation.walkthrough: Take B, U and S from REBELLIOUS ('putting off characters in bus') and 'terribly' rearranges the rest, REELLIO.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lorelei is the siren of Rhine legend whose song lured boatmen to their doom.

clue.text: Scheme artist set up in flat

parts.note: a plan is a scheme

indicators.note: in a down clue set up means raised, read from bottom to top

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword's usual artist

explanation.surface: An artist establishes a scheme in his apartment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns RA into AR; 'in' is a link word. 'flat' looks like an apartment but is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Planar describes something lying in a single plane, two-dimensional and level.

clue.text: Hesitation about open country

indicators.note: about here means turned round, reading backwards

parts.note: er is the sound of hesitation
public means open to all

explanation.surface: Pausing before speaking about the open countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'open country' reads as one phrase but splits: 'open' is wordplay and 'country' the definition; 'about' is the reversal signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A republic is a state or nation without a monarch, a kind of country.

clue.text: Stories about a hospital in Asian city

indicators.note: about means the stories word goes around the other letters

parts.note: lore is traditional stories

explanation.surface: Tales concerning a hospital in an Asian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts LORE around A and H; 'in' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Lahore is a major city in Pakistan, capital of Punjab province.

clue.text: Astrophysicist gives indication of unknown quantity in space

indicators.note: in places the unknown inside the space word

parts.note: a hole is an empty space
y is a standard symbol for an unknown in algebra

explanation.surface: A scientist points to an unknown quantity out in space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'space' looks astronomical but is just a gap, a hole. 'gives indication of' is a link phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Fred Hoyle was a British astrophysicist who coined the phrase Big Bang.

clue.text: Returning agent gets a bit of money — time for share of profits?

indicators.note: returning means coming back, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a rep, or representative, is a sales agent
a cent is a small coin
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: An agent comes back with a small sum, asking if it is time to share the profits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returning' turns REP into PER. 'gets' and 'for' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A percentage is a proportion or cut of earnings, as in a dealer's commission.

clue.text: Inventor making contribution to security in university

definitions.meaning: Linus ... Jr invented the pin-tumbler lock
an Ivy League university in Connecticut

explanation.surface: An inventor helping campus security.
explanation.definitionFit: Linus Yale devised the cylinder lock bearing his name; the same name belongs to an Ivy League college.

clue.text: Push only half the things made for sale

indicators.note: only half keeps just the first four of the eight letters

parts.note: products are goods made to be sold

explanation.surface: Pushing only half the stock out to market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'only half' keeps PROD from PRODUCTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To prod is to poke or nudge, giving a small push.

clue.text: Restaurant serving rubbish is by southern lake

parts.note: rot means nonsense, rubbish
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A lakeside eatery in the south serving junk food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving' and 'by' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotisserie is a restaurant specialising in spit-roasted meats.
